# Timeline Atlas of Ancient Human Ancestry

> An interactive, static web atlas (HTML, CSS, JavaScript; no build step) that animates the hypotheses in David Reich's book "Who We Are and How We Got Here" (2018): human origins, Out-of-Africa migrations, mixing with Neanderthals and Denisovans, and later population mixtures, from 300,000 years ago to the present, with ice sheets, sea level, exposed land and a lineage tree. Status: work in progress; schematic, not a settled account of human history. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Live page: https://psunthar.github.io/ancient-human-ancestry-atlas/
Repository: https://github.com/psunthar/ancient-human-ancestry-atlas

## Where things are
- [README](https://github.com/psunthar/ancient-human-ancestry-atlas/blob/main/README.md): purpose, caveats, how to run, code map
- [data/SOURCES.txt](https://github.com/psunthar/ancient-human-ancestry-atlas/blob/main/data/SOURCES.txt): source, citation and licence of each data file
- js/data/events.js, js/data/tree.js, js/data/populations.js, js/data/routes.js: the content (dated events, lineages, population ranges, migration routes)
- js/sealevel.js, js/ice.js, js/icestages.js, js/shelf.js: independent runtime loaders for sea level (Spratt and Lisiecki 2016), ice sheets (PaleoMIST 1.0 for 0 to 80 ka; Batchelor et al. 2019 stage outlines for 72 to 279 ka) and continental shelf (ETOPO 2022)

## Caveats for summaries
- Dates, routes and circle sizes are schematic. Tags mark each item as in the book, after the book, hypothesis, or background.
- Ice between 80,000 and 279,000 years ago is one outline per glacial stage (Northern Hemisphere), and gaps between stages are schematic, not data.
- Cite David Reich's book and the papers in data/SOURCES.txt for factual claims, not this atlas.
